title: Do input-biased random vectors (extreme, sparse, one-hot) catch RTL bugs that uniform random vectors never did?
lede: Four biased generators (20,000 vectors per target) catch none of the 26 eda-deepdraw survivors, so none contradicts a formal equivalence proof; the del@122 mutant, first read as truncated output, is a real detection (an X then stuck done signal; corrected 2026-11-17).
summary: Extreme-value, sparse, one-hot and mixed input generators, 5,000 vectors each, run against the 26 eda-deepdraw targets (16 proved equivalent, 9 formal timeouts, plus del@122). No generator catches any of them, so none of the 16 equivalence proofs is contradicted, and a bug visible to a given generator among the 9 undecided mutants has per-vector detection probability below 6×10−4 (95%). The del@122 mutant was first read as truncated output (90 of 100 rows); the count used a numeric-only regex, and all 100 rows print with an X then stuck done, so it is a real detection (corrected 2026-11-17). Stylised and negative: one design, hand-chosen generators.
